findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-tenant order retrieval via legacy test endpoint

evidence.why: Order identifier supplied directly from URL route path without validation
Direct query on Orders table by id alone without tenant or user ownership constraint
Returns full order record without post-load owner verification or caller authorization

findings.attack_scenario: An unauthenticated user sends GET /api/v1/test/legacy-orders/{id} with any order ID and receives the complete order entity belonging to another user or tenant.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant data exposure disclosing customer orders, total amount, order description, and owner identity without authentication.
findings.recommendation: Enforce authentication and verify caller ownership and tenant scope using _authzService.AuthorizeAsync before returning order data.

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-tenant order modification via legacy test endpoint

evidence.code: public async Task<ActionResult<Order>> UpdateLegacyOrder(string id, [FromBody] UpdateOrderRequest request)
evidence.why: Target order ID and update payload received from untrusted request body and route parameter
Loads order by primary key without verifying caller identity or tenant
Persists status and description changes without checking caller authorization

data_flow: id path parameter and UpdateOrderRequest body (LegacyTestController.cs:47)
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends PUT /api/v1/test/legacy-orders/{id} with another user's order ID and payload to mutate order description and status without authentication.
findings.impact: Unauthorized modification of customer orders across tenant boundaries, compromising data integrity.
findings.recommendation: Verify caller identity and object ownership using _authzService.AuthorizeAsync with ResourceOperation.Update, returning 404 on authorization failure.
findings.fix_example:
var auth = await _authzService.AuthorizeAsync(User, order, ResourceOperation.Update);
if (!auth.Succeeded) return NotFound();

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-tenant order deletion via legacy test endpoint

evidence.why: Target order ID received from client via URL route parameter without validation
Retrieves order to delete by ID alone with no ownership validation
Removes the order from database without verifying caller ownership

findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends DELETE /api/v1/test/legacy-orders/{id} with any order ID to delete that order across tenants without authentication.
findings.impact: Permanent deletion of order records belonging to any user or tenant, causing severe data loss.
findings.recommendation: Require caller authentication and object-level deletion authorization using _authzService.AuthorizeAsync with ResourceOperation.Delete.

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-tenant order retrieval via Spring legacy test endpoint

evidence.why: Target order ID taken directly from request path variable without validation
Queries database by primary key alone using Spring Data repository without tenant or owner scoping
Returns the fetched order entity without post-load ownership comparison

findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends GET /api/v1/test/legacy-orders/{id} and retrieves any order in the system across all tenants without authentication.
findings.impact: Confidentiality breach exposing customer order records, tenant IDs, and user IDs across tenant boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Enforce ownership verification via securityManager.requireOwnership(order, ResourceOperation.READ) before returning the order entity.

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-tenant order modification via Spring legacy test endpoint

evidence.code: fun updateLegacyOrder(@PathVariable id: String, @RequestBody request: UpdateOrderRequest): ResponseEntity<Any>
evidence.why: Target order ID and updated fields received from untrusted request without validation
Fetches order to mutate by ID alone without verifying ownership or tenant
Saves modified order entity directly without ownership check

data_flow: id path variable and UpdateOrderRequest body (Controllers.kt:185)
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends PUT /api/v1/test/legacy-orders/{id} with modified fields to alter any user's order in any tenant.
findings.impact: Unauthorized tampering and alteration of order status and descriptions across tenant boundaries.

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-tenant order deletion via Spring legacy test endpoint

evidence.why: Target order ID received from client via path variable without validation
Fetches order to delete without tenant or owner verification
Deletes order row from database without verifying caller authorization or ownership

findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends DELETE /api/v1/test/legacy-orders/{id} with any order id and permanently deletes the record without authorization.
findings.impact: Unauthorized deletion of orders across tenants, resulting in permanent data loss.
findings.recommendation: Verify caller ownership via securityManager.requireOwnership(order, ResourceOperation.DELETE) before executing deletion.
findings.fix_example:
val order = orderRepository.findById(id).orElse(null)
securityManager.requireOwnership(order, ResourceOperation.DELETE)
orderRepository.delete(order!!)
return ResponseEntity.noContent().build()

findings.title: Raw SQL query uses string interpolation with unvalidated search query parameter

evidence.code: public async Task<ActionResult<List<Order>>> SearchLegacy([FromQuery] string query)
evidence.why: source: unvalidated query parameter

evidence.code: var rawSql = $"SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE Description LIKE '%{query}%'";
evidence.why: string interpolation directly constructs SQL statement
sink: raw SQL execution without parameter binding

findings.attack_scenario: An unauthenticated caller provides a crafted query parameter to escape the LIKE string literal and inject arbitrary SQL clauses or statements.
findings.impact: Arbitrary SQL execution against the underlying database, allowing an attacker to read, modify, or delete orders across all tenants.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries with FromSqlInterpolated or bind parameters through FormattableString rather than passing interpolated strings to FromSqlRaw.
findings.fix_example: var results = await _dbContext.Orders.FromSqlInterpolated($"SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE Description LIKE {'%' + query + '%'}").ToListAsync();

findings.title: Native SQL query interpolates unvalidated search query parameter

evidence.why: source: unvalidated request parameter

evidence.code: val sql = "SELECT * FROM portal_orders WHERE description LIKE '%$query%'"
evidence.why: string template interpolation directly into SQL string
sink: native query execution without parameter binding

findings.attack_scenario: An unauthenticated caller provides a crafted query parameter containing SQL syntax to break out of the LIKE pattern and manipulate the query structure.
findings.impact: Arbitrary SQL execution in the database, allowing an attacker to read or manipulate records across all tenants.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries with named or positional parameters via Query.setParameter instead of string interpolation.
findings.fix_example: val queryResult = entityManager.createNativeQuery("SELECT * FROM portal_orders WHERE description LIKE :query", OrderEntity::class.java).setParameter("query", "%$query%").resultList
